terms.grammar: relative adverb, with the indicative; answered by totiēns
evidence: Mart. 12.57.28: dormīre quotiēns libuit, īmus ad vīllam
Sen. Ep. 13.2: quī quotiēns cecidit contumācior resurrēxit
terms.comment: For a repeated action Latin puts the quotiēns-clause one step back in time: perfect beside a present (quotiēns libuit, īmus), pluperfect beside an imperfect.

terms.grammar: conjunction, with the indicative: perfect beside a present, pluperfect beside an imperfect
evidence: Cic. Att. 1.6.2: tum dēnique cum illō vēnimus
Cic. Verr. 2.5.27: cum ad aliquod oppidum vēnerat, eādem lectīcā ūsque ad cubiculum dēferēbātur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero’s and Caesar’s usual way (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Ter. Eun. 813: Nōlunt ubi velīs; ubi nōlīs, cupiunt ultrō.
Hor. Ep. 1.14.17: quandōcumque trahunt invīsa negōtia Rōmam (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With the indicative. Lewis & Short: “mostly poet.”

phrases.latin: dormīre quotiēns libuit, īmus ad vīllam
phrases.english: whenever we feel like sleeping, we go to the country
who, every time he fell, got up again more stubborn

phrases.latin: nōs Tusculānō ita dēlectāmur ut nōbīsmet ipsīs tum dēnique cum illō vēnimus placeāmus
phrases.english: I love Tusculum so much that I only like myself when I get there

phrases.latin: Nōlunt ubi velīs; ubi nōlīs, cupiunt ultrō.
phrases.english: When you want them, they won’t; when you don’t, they’re keen of their own accord.

phrases.latin: quandōcumque pilam extrā campum lūsōrium pulsō
phrases.english: whenever I hit the ball out of the ball park
I can catch trout whenever I please.

short-que.html: Hor. Ep. 1.14.17, quandōcumque trahunt invīsa negōtia Rōmam: the first foot is quandō-, the second -cumque tra-, a dactyl, so -que is short, as the enclitic always is.
